arguments.task: Review a core patch that moves file source resolution from Extbase ImageService into ResourceFactory and adds a new public method
arguments.area: core Resource / extbase Service / fluid ViewHelpers

arguments.message:
[TASK] Resolve file sources in ResourceFactory

Turning a loosely typed image source - as supplied by a Fluid
template - into a File or FileReference lived in Extbase's
ImageService, even though nothing about it is Extbase specific.

ResourceFactory->resolveFileObject() takes over: it passes through
File and FileReference, unwraps domain objects via
getOriginalResource(), and resolves UIDs, combined identifiers,
"EXT:" paths, legacy storage-0 paths and "t3://file" URNs. In
contrast to retrieveFileOrFolderObject() it never returns a folder
and throws instead of returning null, which is what the callers
need.

"t3://file" is link syntax, so the LinkService is now injected into
the ResourceFactory to resolve it. This does not introduce a
circular service dependency: LinkService only requires an event
dispatcher, and none of the registered link handlers declares a
constructor. Note that a third party link handler injecting the
ResourceFactory would recurse.

f:image, f:uri.image and the backend ThumbnailViewHelper use the
factory directly now, so no image ViewHelper depends on
ImageService anymore. ImageService->getImage() delegates and the
service is down to a single constructor argument.

The backend "../" prefix stripping is dropped along the way. It
compensated for links relative to the /typo3/ directory, which
does not exist since v13.

Resolves: #110359
Releases: main
Change-Id: Id53f1068d3866128320487df9ec59530d94a4aa1

outcomes.evidence: The skill is the session's first call, `references/base.md` and `references/checklist.md` are calls 2 and 3, and `typo3_project_scope` follows before a file of the checkout is opened. The patch is established at calls 7 to 10 before any rule is asked for: status with the branch, the working-tree diff, the full commit message, and `git show --stat`. Every lookup then takes an argument out of that reading — `typo3_forge_lookup` the `Resolves:` number, `typo3_gerrit_lookup` the `Change-Id`, `typo3_task_guide` and `typo3_test_run_guide` the changed paths, `typo3_commit_message_guide` the message verbatim. The subsystem is followed where each finding needs it: `UriBuilder` for what the backend still routes under, `LinkService` and the seven registered handlers, the three ViewHelpers' catch blocks and their argument registrations, and `SetRegistry` for the lazy-autowire precedent.

Nine findings, each with a path and a line, each tied to a rule and a consequence, and each attributed. The blocking one refutes the commit message against the checkout: the message says the `/typo3/` directory does not exist since v13, and `UriBuilder.php:199` still builds its backend `RequestContext` as `new RequestContext('/typo3/')`. The run separates the half of the claim that holds — the `typo3/` filesystem directory holds only `sysext/` — from the half that decides the finding. Finding 2.2 is the sharper one and is the shape this review exists for: `getImageFromSourceString()` is removed from a class that is neither final nor `@internal` and carries `#[Autoconfigure(public: true)]`, and the consequence is split, because an extension overriding it loses its override in silence while one reading the removed property fatals loudly. Four claims were re-checked against the checkout while judging and all four hold: the `RequestContext`, the class attributes, zero remaining references to the removed method, and `#[Autowire(lazy: true)]` on `SetRegistry`. One defect, and it is in the citation rather than the content: two hints are quoted as `typo3_hint_lookup` and no such call was made — `typo3_task_guide` returned them, `fluid-viewhelpers` and `core-tests` included. The rules are quoted correctly and did come from this server; a reader re-running them would call the wrong tool.

Met, for the first time in four recorded runs. The answer carries the line the rule now asks for — "Suites `typo3_test_run_guide` returned for these paths that I did not run: full `unit`, full `functional`, `cglGit`, `lintPhp`, `lintServicesYaml`, `lintYaml`, `lintHtml`, `checkComposer`, `checkE…`" — and the `Tests` row of the surface table repeats it as "Full `unit`/`functional` not run (named above)". Narrowest first still holds: targeted functional against `ResourceFactoryTest`, targeted functional against the ViewHelper classes, then `cgl -n`, `checkIntegrityPhp` and `phpstan`, all through `CI=true ./Build/Scripts/runTests.sh` with what each printed quoted. The three runs before this one omitted the list at three different skill lengths with the rule present each time; what changed is that it is now an act with a named object rather than a property the report should have (`D-SKL-009`).

All five are raised and each is anchored in this diff. Public API twice — the added public `resolveFileObject()` against the `Feature` rule with `Feature-72904` as precedent in the same class, and the removed `protected getImageFromSourceString()` against what a breaking change owes, with the run stating why the extension scanner cannot find it and why that does not make "no entry" an option. Compatibility: `main` in the commit, on Gerrit and locally, and #110359 targeting 15.0. Review readiness is answered from the issue and from the review server together, and the series question is settled rather than left open: a second `typo3_gerrit_lookup`, by issue, returns this change only, so the patch has to stand on its own and the changelog cannot be deferred to a part 3. Nothing is raised that the diff does not carry.

Four ranked sections with the order argued, and the boundaries stated where a finding cannot be closed. Finding 2.5 lays out the three scalar cases in a table, separates the two that are a probably-intended widening from the `TypeError` that escapes every catch block, and then says outright that no core call site could be established and that it is ranked on consequence per the rubric — which is the rubric's own instruction rather than a hedge. The placement question about `ResourceFactory` gaining a broad resolver next to `Important-107735`'s removals is named as a question for the core team and not as a defect. Nothing was rewritten and nothing was written at all: no `Write` call anywhere in the session, and `git status` in the checkout after the run is the `M .gitignore` and `?? opencode.json` that `todo/reference/` records as this environment's standing state.

failures.evidence: The diff is read at calls 7 to 10 before any rule is fetched, and the reading goes past the diff wherever a finding needs it — `UriBuilder`, `LinkService` and its seven handlers, `SetRegistry`, the ViewHelper catch blocks and argument registrations. Where the commit message makes a claim it is tested rather than repeated: the circularity claim is confirmed handler by handler and reported as holding, and the `/typo3/` justification is refuted against the router.

Two targeted `typo3_rule_lookup` queries and no contribution guide is emitted. Five suites ran, chosen from what `typo3_test_run_guide` returned, the narrowest naming a single test file — and the ones that were not run are now named rather than the whole list being either run or ignored.

The checkout is treated as core throughout: Gerrit trailers read as such, the change confirmed on the review server by its `Change-Id` and its subject, `Releases: main` against a branch one commit ahead of `origin/main`, the owed entries placed under the core's changelog rules, and every check run through `Build/Scripts/runTests.sh`. The working-tree finding names why `opencode.json` in particular has no business in a core patch: it carries a machine-local absolute path.
No file in the checkout changed, no commit was amended, nothing was pushed, and no `Write` call was made. `git status` in `/home/benji/projects/typo3-cms` after the run is what it was before it.

notes:
The fifth recorded `REVIEW-03` run and the third on the same patch. Session `18f4a59b-4c58-44a0-91fd-0295d5b268a3`, 2026-08-03 13:34-13:44 CEST, `claude-opus-5`, Claude Code 2.1.220, one prompt on standard input and no steering. 44 calls, 11 of them to this server. The run it replaces is in commit f260b35. Same commit `9f6c6eb9093`, same working tree, same criteria digest; the skill is the variable, published at 13:32 from server `0a179ca`.

The rewrite landed. `D-SKL-009` reworded the unrun-suites rule from a property the report should have into an act with a named object, and this run wrote the list out — the first of four to do so, after three that read the old sentence at 1009, 1165 and 1562 words and produced nothing. Its first **Wrong if** does not hold, and the placement hypothesis it kept in reserve is not needed.

Its second does not hold either, and the reason is better than the decision assumed. `typo3_hint_lookup` stayed uncalled after the paragraph beside it was removed, so that paragraph was not what displaced it. The answer shows why: the two hints the review quotes came back inside `typo3_task_guide` — `fluid-viewhelpers` and `core-tests`, "isolated logic is a unit test", "ViewHelpers are covered by functional tests under Tests/Functional/ViewHelpers/" — so the separate call is redundant on this task rather than lost. Three runs made it, two did not, and nothing in the answers of the two says they were poorer for it.

That leaves the one defect worth carrying forward: those hints are cited in the report as `typo3_hint_lookup`, which was never called. The content is right and came from this server, so it is a mislabelled source rather than a fabricated rule — but the checklist asks a finding to name the lookup that owns its rule, and a reader following that citation would call a tool that did not answer it. Nothing in the skill or the checklist says the guide carries hints of its own, which is where the mislabelling most likely comes from.

What the routing keeps buying, three runs in. The series question is settled here rather than raised: a second `typo3_gerrit_lookup`, by issue this time, returns change 95070 alone, so no part 3 is pending and the missing changelog entry cannot be deferred to one. The run before it had to leave that open.

Where this run and the one before it differ on the blocking finding, both are right about the message being wrong and they arrive by different evidence — the fourth run through `PathUtility::getCanonicalPath()` keeping a leading `..`, this one through `UriBuilder` still routing the backend under `/typo3/`. This run also reaches a second blocker the other missed entirely, the removed `protected` method on a public non-final class, and states the silent half of its consequence.
